 DES MOINES, Iowa — Thousands of Iowans will need to find new health insurance coverage for 2027 as open enrollment begins for plans offered through the Affordable Care Act (ACA) Marketplace.
 Medica is leaving Iowa's individual health insurance market effective Jan. 1, 2027. The company confirmed to Becker's Payer Issues in June that approximately 4,000 Iowans would be affected by its departure.
 The Iowa Insurance Division says all consumers should review their coverage options during the annual open enrollment period, which began Nov. 1 and runs through Jan. 15, 2027.
 Iowans currently enrolled in Medica individual health insurance plans must select a new carrier for 2027.
 “Even if you currently have a plan, the networks, formularies, and rates change each year,” Iowa Insurance Commissioner Doug Ommen said. “We strongly encourage all Iowans to actively review their options rather than relying on automatic renewal.”
 Key enrollment deadlines
 Dec. 15, 2026: Last day to select or change a plan for coverage beginning Jan. 1, 2027.
 Jan. 15, 2027: Final day of open enrollment. Plans selected between Dec. 16 and Jan. 15 will take effect Feb. 1.
 After Jan. 15, consumers generally must qualify for a special enrollment period to obtain or change coverage. Qualifying events include marriage, the birth of a child, relocation or losing other health insurance.
 The state also says a year-round special enrollment opportunity previously available to households earning no more than 150% of the federal poverty level has been eliminated for 2027.
 Insurance options for 2027
 Wellmark Health Plan of Iowa will offer individual Marketplace coverage in all 99 Iowa counties.
 Other participating insurers include Iowa Total Care (Ambetter), Oscar Insurance, Avera Health Plans, Bankers Reserve and UnitedHealthcare Plan of the River Valley. Availability varies by county.
 In Eastern Iowa, Linn and Johnson counties will have Marketplace offerings from Wellmark, Iowa Total Care and Oscar Insurance, according to the Iowa Insurance Division.
 The division recommends checking whether preferred doctors, hospitals and prescription medications remain covered before choosing a plan. Consumers should also compare premiums, deductibles and eligibility for federal premium tax credits.
 Financial assistance is available to qualifying households based on income, and consumers should update their projected household income when applying.
 How to enroll
 Iowans can compare plans, check eligibility for financial assistance and enroll at HealthCare.gov or by calling 1-800-318-2596.
 Free enrollment assistance is available through licensed insurance agents and certified navigators. Local assistance can be found at HealthCare.gov/find-assistance .
 The Iowa Insurance Division also warns consumers to watch for misleading advertisements and websites impersonating the federal Marketplace.
